surface: An injury’s notice
where: Home’s notices, the moment it happens (Go There opens Papers)
why: Read as the pressure student met a sprain, and every kind on a student and an uninsured New Yorker in turn. It gave its days but no date, put the bill before what the injury keeps you from, said “2 sessions”, and “Call In Sick, on School, excuses a day of classes while it mends” read as one day in all, where Call In Sick can be pressed on any day it mends, and it didn’t say the button is on School’s Classes tab or that it excuses the whole day at school (classes, calls and a shift), as its tooltip says. A billed injury said “You owe $699.13 for its care.” without saying what the care was. A laid-up injury didn’t say the School excuses what it keeps you from on its own, and a cut or a knock didn’t say it keeps you from nothing. The title names the injury, so the body opens on how long it takes, as before.
changes: In order: “It takes 7 days to mend, until September 19, 2026.”, then what it keeps you from and what to do (“Until then you can’t work out, and it holds back the physical side of your work. Each day until then, Call In Sick, on School’s Classes tab, can excuse that day at school.”, or “You’re laid up until then, kept from classes, work and training. What you miss at school is excused.”, or “It won’t stop you working out or going to class.”), then the cost, the care named in both kinds (“You owe $699.13 for its care, a visit to urgent care and two sessions of physical therapy.”). The middle is one function, `injuryKeeps`, which the look says too.

evidence.ref: tests/language-injury.test.ts: 'an injury says the day it mends, and what it keeps you from in each kind'
tests/evidence-g07-life.test.ts: 'a work-study crew shift that pulls a muscle is work'

surface: An injury’s look, and Mending on your look
where: How You Are on Home, or your name: your look, then An Injury
why: Its way in promises “What it is, when it mends, and what it keeps you from.” A knock’s and a cut’s look gave only the day, so the promise went unanswered; a broken bone’s didn’t say the classes it keeps you from are excused; and a sprain’s ended on the same one-day-sounding Call In Sick line as the notice. The Condition way under it says plainly that an injury doesn’t lower condition but adds stress and lowers morale each day, the distinction players miss, and stays.
changes: The summary after “It mends by …” is the notice’s own middle (`injuryKeeps`), in the person’s pronouns: a laid-up injury adds “What you miss at school is excused.” for the player at the School, a cut or a knock says “It won’t stop you working out or going to class.”, and Call In Sick says where it is and that it can excuse each day at school.

evidence.ref: tests/language-injury.test.ts: 'says a laid-up student’s classes are excused, and a knock keeps you from nothing'

surface: The flu
where: Home’s notices, the week it strikes; your look while it lasts
why: Read as the pressure student met it three times (October, February, October) and seen and unseen on a student and a New Yorker. The unseen notice said “You have the flu.” under the title You Have The Flu; it said “Work Out waits until it passes”; it never said the flu holds back the work you show while it lasts, which the Player Profile’s Readiness Today says (“The flu holds back your voice and body work”) and the feedback names; and Call In Sick “excuses a day of classes” read as one day of five, without saying where the button is. Seen at urgent care it opened on the bill’s line, “The flu, at urgent care, PhysicianOne …”. While it lasted no look said you had it: your look showed an injury’s Mending line and nothing for the flu.
changes: Unseen: “It lasts until August 29, 2026, and it has cost you some condition and energy. Until it passes you can’t work out, and it holds back your voice and body work. Each day until then, Call In Sick, on School’s Classes tab, can excuse that day at school. You didn’t see a doctor, so there’s nothing to pay.” Seen: “You saw a doctor for it at PhysicianOne Urgent Care (…), New Haven.” first. Your look gains “Ill. The flu, until August 29, 2026.” while it lasts.

evidence.ref: tests/language-care17.test.ts: 'the flu, as a student meets it'
tests/evidence-g05-life.test.ts: 'the flu, seen at urgent care, is five days'
tests/evidence-g30-ui.test.ts: 'takes the flu’s 25 condition and 30 energy'

surface: Care had: a doctor’s visit, the emergency room, a stay in hospital
where: Home’s notices, when the care is had (Go There opens Papers)
why: Each began with the bill’s own line as a fragment, “A doctor’s visit, Yale Health Center, Student Health.”, “The emergency room, Yale New Haven Hospital, …”, “A stay in hospital, …, for 3 days.”, a log entry where a sentence about what happened belongs. A marketplace claim denied was told “You owe $45.00.” in the visit’s notice over a bill of the full $183.98, the next notice alone giving the right figure: the words disagreed with the bill. The due sentence (“It’s taken from your checking account on …, and if there isn’t enough then, it becomes medical debt.”) says the date, the account and the consequence, and stays; so do the bills’ names on Papers.
changes: “You saw a doctor at Yale Health Center, Student Health.”, “You saw a doctor for a review of your asthma at …”, “You saw a doctor to renew your prescription at …”, “You saw the specialist your doctor referred you to at …” (`seenWords`, an older save’s wording said as before); “You went to the emergency room at …”; “You’re in hospital for 3 days at …”, the practice’s name last since names hold commas. A denied claim’s visit says “You owe the full $183.98, because your plan denied the claim.”, the bill’s figure, drawn on the same keyed draw before the notice instead of after it.

evidence.ref: tests/language-care17.test.ts: 'a marketplace claim denied, told in its visit’s notice at the bill’s figure'

surface: A doctor’s appointment: booked, missed, not seen, a referral
where: Home’s notices; the calendar’s stop; Papers, Health Cover: Book An Appointment, Call It Off
why: Missed and not seen opened on the label and a colon, “A doctor’s visit: you weren’t there, so you weren’t seen.”, a telegraphic fragment. The refusals of Book An Appointment and Call It Off name the obstacle plainly.
changes: “You weren’t there for your doctor’s appointment, so you weren’t seen.” and “You weren’t seen for your doctor’s appointment at Yale Health Center, Student Health.”, each kind of appointment said as a noun phrase (`appointmentWords`: “the review of your asthma”, “your appointment with the specialist”). surface: Public cover over the months: ended, renewed, changed, ending
where: Home’s notices on a month’s first; Papers, Health Cover
why: Read in care-after.txt for a dropped plan, a status lost and a renewal by age and by SNAP. Each says what happened, from when, why, and the next step with its window (“You have 60 days to enroll in the marketplace”, or “Dropping a plan or leaving it unpaid doesn’t open special enrollment.”), and Your Health Cover Ended adds California’s penalty where it applies. The legal conditions stay exact, as the style guide asks of official notices.

surface: Medicaid’s work rules: a notice of noncompliance, approved, denied, a hardship
where: Home’s notices; Papers, Health Cover: Request A Hardship Exception
why: The longest notice in the area, read whole: it goes in the order a player needs, what wasn’t found and in which months, the day you stay covered to, what you needn’t send and the one thing you can (a stay in hospital, with the button’s name), what happens on which day if you don’t answer, and what follows for the tax credit and a new application. Every part is a deadline or a consequence the brief says never to hide, so it stays whole.

surface: Your wellbeing: your look and the eight measures
where: How You Are on Home, or your name: your look, then each measure’s look
why: Read in every band and save. The distinction players most confuse is said where it’s needed: Energy’s look says energy is today’s and only sleep brings it back, that stamina is something else (how long you keep going in a long scene) and so is condition; Fitness says it is the Player Profile’s Stamina, built by working out, and that rest brings back energy and condition, not fitness; Condition says illness wears it down and an injury doesn’t, and that health (a long-term condition, cover and care) is on Papers. Each band’s sentence says what that figure does now. Two footnotes were fragments: seven measures’ “From 0 to 100. It changes with every hour the clock runs.”

surface: A trait’s look
where: Your look: each trait you chose
why: It shows the trait’s description, what it changes as a table of its own figures beside the figure all your traits make together, and its cost, so a player can see why a trait matters without the engine’s knobs; a trait that changes no figure says so in a sentence.

surface: The training classes named

surface: The places: the gazetteer’s names and notes
where: Creation’s birthplace and home; Home’s Where You Are; a place’s look

Two of GeoNames’ names fall short and are reported, not edited, since the table is generated: Cambodia’s “Riels” (brief 15’s finding) and “Aland Islands” for Åland.

surface: Actor or Actress

surface: The engine’s own checks
where: Never a player screen: a developer’s error if the engine breaks its own rules
why: These are internal faults (a decider that reads nothing, a ledger that doesn’t balance, an empty list drawn from) that only a test or a broken build meets; a player who meets a failed command reads the frame’s own “That didn’t go through because of an error in the game.” instead.
